target_text: The Duska male line is from Senné; Iňačovce enters through a wife's family.
note: The places do not pick a side yet. They do explain why the two villages pair up: both were Vécsey villages, under 4 km apart, and the Roman Catholics of Iňačovce belonged to the Senné parish. A marriage between the two was a short walk inside one estate, and would be entered at Senné if the couple were Latin-rite.
try: Read the 1715 and 1720 tax lists for both villages first (PL-R-020). Senné had 5 and then 11 households, Iňačovce 8 and then 11, so a surname is either there or it arrived later. For baptisms before 1866 use the older Senné volumes (PL-R-006): the catalogued title (PL-R-001) starts baptisms only in 1866.

target_text: The Duskas were Roman Catholic and the Demkos Greek Catholic.
note: This is the pattern the parish map predicts: Senné was the Latin parish with the only school a Roman Catholic one, Iňačovce the Greek Catholic parish. The caution is now a number. In 1851 Senné had 580 Roman Catholics and 238 Greek Catholics, and in 1904 it had 484 and 231. Close to a third of the village was Greek Catholic, and those families are in the Iňačovce book (PL-H-001). A village does not fix a rite.
try: Check both books for one event. For a mixed couple see the coordinator's X-A-001: search the Senné register and the Iňačovce one.

target_text: The record cited as the 1869 census does not come from the standard FamilySearch Slovakia collection.
note: Three reports now place Ung county's 1869 sheets in the Zakarpattia archive, one of them giving the Berehove branch, fond 7/2, and one stating outright that FamilySearch has not filmed them. An 1869 sheet for Senné would have to come from there, directly or through a hired researcher.
try: Ask the owner how the image reached him, once the line is processed. A Berehove call number would settle DUS:H-007 and PL-H-006 together.

target_text: Jozef Duska of Senné no. 73 (1930) is not Ahn 8.
note: No evidence either way, but the test is within reach. The 1930 sheets are in the Slovak National Archives and are shown online. Senné had 171 houses in 1940, so number 73 is a real house in the older part of the numbering.
try: Pull house 73 from the 1930 census online (PL-R-025) and read the absent-member notes.

target_text: The copy-book belongs to the Roman Catholic parish of Senné itself.
note: The place evidence is stronger than at the first batch. Štefan Rácz was parish priest of Senné from 1831 to 1841, so a Senné copy-book for 1837 to 1840 would be his. The Kulin family were landlords at Kisszeretva, and Kisszeretva was a filial of Senné about 1799 and in 1917 (PL-H-003, now supported). The parish sat in the Middle Ung deanery district of the Szatmár diocese. None of this rules out a neighbouring parish.
try: Look for the name Rácz, as copyist or signatory, on the ten pages. The title board of the film item still decides it.

target_text: The immigrant generation reached Canada between 1924 and 1930.
note: Senné had two leaving waves: 1870 to 1890, and 1910 to 1930, mostly to the United States, with many returning to buy land. After 1921 the Vécsey estate was sold off in parcels at several times the official price, families took mortgages, and the 1929 slump caught them. That is a village-level reason to leave in the late 1920s. It says nothing about one family.
try: Nothing to run here. Keep it as background for whatever the passenger lists show.

target_text: A c. 1754 urbarial record where the household kept two beehives.
note: The published urbarial tables for Szenna name four landlords and count 26 villein households; they do not count hives. See PL-H-007: the record may be a tax conscription.
try: Record the heading and call number when the image arrives.

target_text: Maria Demko was baptised Greek Catholic.
note: If she was of Iňačovce, Greek Catholic is the likeliest rite: it was the parish church and the larger school. But Iňačovce also had a Reformed congregation with its own school (41 pupils in 1916) and a church built in 1912. A Reformed Demko would be in the Reformed register at Prešov, which runs to 1940, and nothing would be in Uzhhorod.
try: Before the Uzhhorod search, rule out the Reformed book (PL-R-005). It is the cheaper check.

target_text: Maria Demko was born in a village now in Slovakia, not Ukraine.
note: An Uzhhorod record does not point east of the border. Uzhhorod was the county town for both villages and the seat of the bishop over the Iňačovce parish. See PL-H-005.
try: Check whether Solymos is in the Mukachevo eparchy series for the Ung district (PL-R-004).

target_text: The Uzhhorod record is a Greek Catholic register or duplicate of the Mukachevo eparchy.
note: The catalogued series covers 1826 to 1938 and the Prešov run for Iňačovce stops at 1898, so the gap is exactly where a birth of about 1899 to 1912 would fall.
try: As PL-N-011. If Solymos is listed, note the film numbers for her birth window.

target_text: If born after 1 October 1895, a civil birth registration exists for her.
note: The date is right: Law XXXIII of 1894 took effect on 1 October 1895. Books pass from the registry office to the state archive 100 years after their last entry, so a birth book closed before about 1926 should now be in an archive.
try: Find which registry office served Iňačovce and which served Senné. That is still open on this page too.

target_text: Settling whether the Demkos were Rusyn will need a language or nationality column.
lean: supports the owner's lean, at village level only
note: The 1734 visitation says Rusyn was spoken in the Greek Catholic parish of Iňačovce. The village was nearly empty in 1715 and was refilled after 1720 from the north of Ung and Zemplín, Belá nad Cirochou among the places named. So the Greek Catholic community there has a recorded Rusyn-speaking start. That is a fact about the parish, not about one family.
try: The 1930 census sheet for the household gives nationality as declared (PL-R-025). Compare it with the 1734 note, not with the surname.

target_text: The Demkos are the Iňačovce side of the family.
note: Nothing found on surnames by village; this agent does not search names. The places only say that either village could hold a Greek Catholic family (PL-H-001).
try: The 1715 and 1720 lists for both villages (PL-R-020) and the 1930 sheets for Iňačovce (PL-R-025).

target_text: Mihaly Duska and Maria Demko married in the old country between 1908 and 1935.
note: Where to look depends on the rites. By custom a wedding was held in the bride's parish (from training, unchecked): Iňačovce if she was Greek Catholic of either village, Senné if both were Latin-rite. From October 1895 there is a state register entry as well, whatever the church.
try: Search the civil marriage books first; they do not depend on guessing the rite.

target_text: The Demkos are the Iňačovce side of the family.
note: A Greek Catholic family did not have to live in Iňačovce to be in the Iňačovce book. Senné itself had 238 Greek Catholics in 1851 and 231 in 1904, and the Iňačovce parish chronicle counts 245 in Senné. Jastrabie and Stretava belonged to the same parish district. So 'Senné and Iňačovce' in family memory can mean one household in Senné that went to church in Iňačovce.
try: In any Iňačovce Greek Catholic entry, read the residence column before assuming the village.

target_text: The Uzhhorod record is a Greek Catholic register or register duplicate of the Mukachevo eparchy.
note: The Iňačovce Greek Catholic church archive was badly damaged by lightning on 6 July 1929 and by fire on 1 April 1930. The indexed register stops in 1898. If the parish's own later books were lost or spoiled, a copy held by the bishop or the county would be the surviving record, which fits a search ending in Uzhhorod. This is filed under X-Q-01.
try: Ask the parish or the Košice eparchy archive which volumes after 1898 survive. That is a place question; this agent will take it if the coordinator agrees.

target_text: The strip is cut from a Greek Catholic baptism register.
note: The place evidence names the book: the Greek Catholic register of Čičarovce, Prešov catalogue no. 182, births 1857-1886, film 40-41 (PL-H-009, PL-R-050). Vysoká was a filial of that parish from 1806, and Ján Csurgovics was its priest from 1882 to 1886, after Jozef Kubek, which is the order of the signatures on your strips.
try: For the reused-name rule (X-017): the burials for Viszoka from 1882 are in the same volume to 1886, and in no. 182/1 from 1887 to 1907. Those are the two volumes to search for the fifteen years after the 1882 baptism.

target_text: György Demkó and Mária Hreskó of Viszoka no. 132 are Maria Demko's parents.
note: The mother in that household is entered as Roman Catholic. The Roman Catholics of Viszoka belonged to Pavlovce nad Uhom, not to Čičarovce. A child of the couple entered on the mother's side would be in the Pavlovce Roman Catholic book (PL-R-052), and so would the mother's own baptism and burial.
try: Search Pavlovce as the other rite's parish. Its filmed run is 1818-1907; one index shows no births there between 1828 and 1868.

target_text: If born after 1 October 1895, a civil birth registration exists for her.
note: Your own DM-D-008 answers the question I had left open: in August 1906 the civil registrar for Solymos signed at Alsókánya, which is Jastrabie pri Michalovciach (PL-P-014). I have not confirmed the identification of Alsókánya from a gazetteer; it rests on the parish list of 1917 and the 1939 protocol, which both pair the two names.
try: Ask for the Jastrabie registry district's birth books. The 1906 volume passed the 100-year mark in 2006 and should be in a state archive.

target_text: György Demko of Gönyű no. 24 is the same man as György Demkó of Viszoka.
note: The two places are about 60 km apart, in different counties (Abaúj-Torna and Ung) and, for Greek Catholics, different eparchies (Prešov and Mukachevo). The research pass found no shared landlord, estate or documented movement between the Košice villages and the Uh valley. That is distance, not proof; X-009 applies.
try: Nothing place-based will settle this. The Belža register (PL-R-053) for a marriage of the Gönyű couple would.

target_text: György Demko of Gönyű 24 is a different man from György Demkó of Viszoka 132.
note: See PL-N-022: about 60 km, two counties, two eparchies, no documented link found. Your reading of Folder 3 as Belža is supported (PL-H-010): Gönyű and Szina were Greek Catholic filials of Bölzse from the 1770s, and the Belža register for 1791-1896 is in the Košice state archive.
try: The '-falva' village is one of three candidates, all now part of Valaliky (PL-H-011, PL-P-054). Check the surviving letters against Bernátfalva, Búzafalva and Csontosfalva.

target_text: Two baptism strips of about 1887 with residences read as Sztrajnyán and Lasztomér.
note: Both identifications hold. Sztrajnyán is a recorded Hungarian form of Stráňany, a village joined to Michalovce in 1925. Its Greek Catholics were in the Michalovce Greek Catholic parish (no. 673 for 1876-1890) and its Roman Catholics in the Michalovce Roman Catholic parish (no. 667 for births 1883-1895). Lastomír had a Greek Catholic register of its own from 1860 (no. 531); its Roman Catholics went to Michalovce and its Reformed had their own parish (no. 534). PL-H-013, PL-R-055, PL-R-056.
try: An entry made 'by mistake' at Sztrajnyán points to the other Michalovce book: if the form in hand is Greek Catholic, look in the Roman Catholic no. 667, and the reverse. The entry number it should carry, 95, is the thing to match. For Lasztomér, if no. 531 fails, try Šamudovce no. 1217.

target_text: A soldier's card naming Enyiczke, Abaúj-Torna.
note: Enyiczke is Haniska by Košice. It lay in the same county as Belža, Gyňov and Seňa, so this card belongs with the Abaúj group under X-Q-04, not with Ung. I have not put it on the map: the one position I found for it disagrees with where I recall the village to be. The epidemic cemetery at Barca of March 1915 is entered as PL-E-012; a web search found nothing on it.
try: Nothing place-based.

target_text: Fifty-eight strips from the Iňačovce Greek Catholic book, 1814 to 1896.
note: The archive's catalogue lets each strip be placed in a volume by its year: no. 380 for 1811-1831, no. 381 for 1831-1859, no. 382 for births 1861-1870, no. 383 for births 1870-1898. The languages it gives for the volumes match your run by year. Births of 1860 are in no listed volume. The catalogue's district is Iňačovce, Jastrabie, Senné and Stretava; it puts Stretavka under Slavkovce, so your Kis Szeretva entry of about 1871 is an exception worth a second look.
try: Burials are in the same four volumes, which is where the fifteen-year search under X-017 goes for any child of the parish. The Slovak note of 1934 means the 1870-1898 volume was in an office then; a registry office stamp or a later certificate number on any strip would say which.

target_text: The couple entered as Krak are a Bodnár husband and his wife; the man is once entered under his wife's name.
note: I looked for a documented custom of a man being entered under his wife's or his house's name in these villages and found nothing specific to them. Slovak onomastics does describe unofficial 'living names', among them a name taken from the house, but the studies found are for western and central Slovakia. Treat it as a possibility that suggests a test, no more.
try: The same question for your Szenna 31 and Solymos 31 entries, and for the Jesztreb household at seven house numbers: I found nothing on renumbering in Ung county. A cadastral map or the 1869 census sheets would settle whether numbers were reissued.

target_text: The copy-book belongs to the Roman Catholic parish of Senné itself and was filmed with the Senné register.
note: The archive's catalogue describes Senné volume no. 1090, marriages 1863-1886, as also holding notes by the bishop of Szatmár for 1837-1840, written from the reverse side of the book. Your ten pages are of those years. That is the Senné register, and it names the volume: no. 1090, microfilm 287 (PL-H-014, supported at 80).
try: On film 1793682, go to the end of the Senné marriages of 1863-1886 and look for pages bound the other way up. That would give the image numbers asked for in RQ-4 without waiting for the owner.

target_text: Michal Duska was born at Senné between 1895 and 1908 and baptised in its Roman Catholic church.
note: Your question answered from the catalogue. No. 1089 is one volume of 254 leaves holding births from 1866 to 1912, with no gap noted, so a Senné Roman Catholic baptism of 1895 to 1908 should be in it. Marriages from 1887 to 1926 are in no. 1092, so a marriage of 1915 to 1926 is at Prešov; one of 1927 to 1929 is not. A birth in those years also has a state entry from October 1895.
try: If the baptism is not in no. 1089, the Greek Catholic volume no. 383 of Iňačovce (births 1870-1898) is the other book for a Senné child born to 1898.

target_text: A candidate baptism for Maria Demko's mother: Mária Kocsis, born 1887, Solymos 19.
note: For the burial search that would lift or sink it. To 1898: Iňačovce volume no. 383, where the remarks column of the baptism entry is the first place to look, as you found. From October 1895: the state death register of the office that served Solymos, which sat at Alsókánya in 1906. That register covers the eight years after 1898 that you counted as uncovered. I cannot open the register images from here.
try: Ask the registry office or state archive that holds the Jastrabie district's death books for 1895 to 1906.

target_text: The book these 45 strips come from is the Reformed register for Iňačovce kept within the Lúčky parish.
note: Ruled here as PL-H-017, supported at 85. The catalogue's no. 592/1 is a register kept for the Iňačovce filial alone, births 1819 to 1927; your strips run 1825 to 1921 and are all Solymos. On your question about Pályin: the catalogue gives Palín its own Reformed register from 1806 and its own district, and puts Iňačovce under Lúčky. Nothing read here makes Solymos a filial of Palín in 1837, so the Pályin preacher is best read as a neighbour standing in. On 'Solymos 152': the village had 119 houses in 1828 and 190 in 1940, so the number is possible.
try: A marriage or burial of the same families is in the same volume: marriages 1820-1926, deaths 1819-1936.

target_text: Ahn 8 is the Mihály born in [1902] at a place written 'Bradenville'.
note: The place is real: Bradenville is a coal town in Derry Township, Westmoreland County, Pennsylvania, two miles from Latrobe. People from the Greek Catholic lands were there at the date: about thirty families founded a Greek Catholic parish in 1902. I found no Hungarian Reformed congregation at Bradenville; the nearest found are Pittsburgh (1890) and Johnstown (1900). So your recollection of the place holds, and where the child was baptised in America is not established. This says nothing about who the child is (X-009). Update at PL-B-009: you have refuted DUS:H-040, so this is no longer about the line. The place stands as evidence of where people of Solymos went.
try: The remark says the entry was made from an extract of a birth certificate. A Pennsylvania birth of 1902 predates statewide registration, so the extract was probably a county or church paper; the county is Westmoreland. That last sentence is recalled, not sourced.

target_text: The family on the compiled chart, with a birth of 1906 read as Passaic (?), are Demkos of Vysoká nad Uhom.
note: Passaic fits the period in general: Slovaks were there from 1879, it had textile mills, and it had one of the first Greek Catholic parishes in America, founded in 1890. Families going out and coming back within a few years were common. I found nothing that names Vysoká nad Uhom, or any Uh valley village, at Passaic. My one emigration fact for Vysoká is from its municipal history and concerns the 1930s.
try: If the chart's 1906 birth is real, the Greek Catholic parish of St Michael at Passaic is the book to ask.

target_text: Ninety-five strips from the Senné Roman Catholic baptism book, 1866 to 1912.
note: The book is Prešov catalogue no. 1089. The catalogue says it holds births 1866-1912 on 254 pages and has the priests' names inside the binding; your strips open with that list and have page 212 at April 1905. Your FamilySearch path and image number belong on the same volume. The fire of 28 October 1865 in that list may be why the book begins in 1866 (PL-H-018, open at 40).
try: Your marriage entry of 1892: 'Hrabó' is the farmstead Hrabov, named in the 1930 census summary you sent, which is why it has no house number. 'Iske' is Ižkovce, in the Greek Catholic parish of Čičarovce; a Greek Catholic born there before 1887 is in Čičarovce nos. 180 to 182.

target_text: The Roman Catholic baptism of a woman of Solymos, to be found in her own church's book.
note: The Roman Catholics of Solymos belonged to the Senné parish throughout: a filial of Szenna in 1799, and in the Senné parish district in the archive's catalogue. Her baptism is in the Senné Roman Catholic book. If she was born in 1866 or later it is in no. 1089. If earlier, it is in a volume the state archive does not hold, and a fire of October 1865 may be the reason (PL-H-018).
try: Her marriage and burial are easier: Senné marriages 1863-1886 are no. 1090 and deaths 1831-1886 no. 1091.

target_text: The Uzhhorod record is the county copy of the state registration of 1906.
note: What I can cite: the Zakarpattia archive at Uzhhorod holds 3,382 state register books for 1895 to 1937 in its fond 1606, beside 1,788 church books. In 1913 Solymos was in the notary district of Alsókánya. What I cannot cite: that the second copies for villages which stayed in Czechoslovakia are among them. The research pass found no statement either way. My own entry for this reading, PL-H-015, is now at 65.
try: The printed union catalogue of register books for Zakarpattia (2009) lists the fond village by village. It could not be opened. It is the finding aid that would settle this.

target_text: Where a marriage of 30 January 1927 between a Roman Catholic of Senné and a Greek Catholic of Iňačovce would be registered.
note: In a church book and in a state book. Church: the Senné Roman Catholic marriages at Prešov end in 1926 (no. 1092), so a marriage of January 1927 at Senné is in the next volume, which is not in the archive; the Iňačovce Greek Catholic volumes after 1898 are not located at all. State: the marriage register of the office for the village where it was held. Senné's office today is Palín, and the 1930 census summary for Senné was signed at Palín; Solymos was in the notary district of Alsókánya in 1913. Which office held the 1927 book I have not found.
try: Ask the registry office at Palín for the entry of 30 January 1927, under both the church volume and the state register. The 1947 certificate you hold shows the Senné parish was still issuing from its own books then.
